gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-pathway-extreme: Pathway Extreme reads modern and tidy, with a big x-height and short stubby ascenders. Stencilia's gappy, structural display letters make the clearest impression, and that sharp difference is what holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear has a lofty x-height and wide open mouths. Stencilia above it brings spacious gaps at its curve terminals and a compact, striking, structural look, so the heading draws attention while the plain sans below stays easy to follow.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-prompt: Stencilia opens with structural, striking letters, their curves left spacious at the terminals, and Prompt follows with oversized small letters. One announces, the other simply talks.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-pt-sans-caption: Bold structure up top, then open-bowled warmth. PT Sans Caption has big-bodied lowercase and inviting, unclosed bowls, so a long stretch of text under Stencilia's striking heading would read in a contemporary, professional voice.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-puritan: Approachable is the word for Puritan, whose rounded forms stay open to the side and whose e and a counters look oversized. Stencilia handles the structural, striking announcement; Puritan handles the talking.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-questrial: Stencil-cut flatness meets a tall, wire-like line. Questrial is monoline while Stencilia is not, so shrinking the heading would lose its gappy curve terminals.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-radio-canada: Contemporary in feel, Radio Canada stands its c, s and z tall and full, drawn as a steady, unmodulated line. Stencilia's gappy structure is the louder voice.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big fills the line with a tall x-height and wire-like monoline strokes, its terminals finishing well clear of the stem. Under Stencilia, a long passage would feel neutral, steady and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-readex-pro: Professional in tone, Stencilia pairs structural, striking display letters with spacious gaps at its curve terminals. Readex Pro answers with horizontals exactly as heavy as its verticals, giving the page a calm, unvarying weight.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-roboto: Roboto has generous mouths on its round letters. Stencilia does striking, structural display work with spacious curve gaps, while the sans body stays clean and contemporary, doing the quiet job of carrying the words.
